name: Selin
presentingProblem: I keep ending up in the same kind of relationship — I get really attached, then the person pulls away and I fall apart. It's happened three times now.
backstory: Selin is a marketing executive. She was raised by a father who was emotionally unavailable and a mother who was loving but overprotective. She has an anxious attachment style. She describes her relationships as 'intense at first, then they cool off and I go crazy trying to keep them close.' She has a history of sending many messages when a partner doesn't respond quickly. She is intelligent and self-aware enough to notice the pattern but cannot stop it.
disorderProfile: Recurrent depressive episodes in relational context

coreBeliefs: I have to work very hard to keep someone interested in me
intermediateBeliefs: If he doesn't reply quickly, he's losing interest
I need to fix things immediately or the relationship will end
Being alone means I am worthless
automaticThoughts: Why hasn't he replied? He must be angry at me
I need to call him — I can't handle this uncertainty
Maybe if I'm more interesting/fun/available, he'll stay
triggers: Discussion of her attachment behaviors (messaging, checking)
Exploring her fear of being alone
defenses: Pleasing (agreeing readily, trying to give 'good' answers)
Minimization (downplaying the severity of her behavior)
